text:
## Observations

1. Each maximal run of ones starts at a `1` that is either the first character or immediately follows a `0`. The run ends just before the next `0` or at the end of the string.
2. Between the (K−1)-th and K-th 1-blocks there is a nonempty run of zeros. Moving the K-th block swaps it with that run of zeros.
3. The prefix through the end of the (K−1)-th block and the suffix after the K-th block keep their original contents. The suffix is empty if the K-th block reaches the end of the string.
4. Only three boundaries are needed to assemble the answer, and the four pieces of the result have a combined length of N.

## Solution sketch

> Each maximal run of ones starts at a `1` that is either the first character or immediately follows a `0`. The run ends just before the next `0` or at the end of the string.

1. Read N, K, and S. Scan S from left to right, counting 1-blocks at their starts. Record the position just after the (K−1)-th block, the start of the K-th block, and the position just after the K-th block. Use N as the position just after a block that reaches the end of S, with positions counted from zero. Stop once all three boundaries are known. The input guarantee ensures both blocks exist.

> Between the (K−1)-th and K-th 1-blocks there is a nonempty run of zeros. Moving the K-th block swaps it with that run of zeros.

2. Take the K-th block from its start up to the position just after it. Take the intervening zeros from the position just after the (K−1)-th block up to the start of the K-th block. Put the K-th block before those zeros so that it joins the preceding block.

> The prefix through the end of the (K−1)-th block and the suffix after the K-th block keep their original contents. The suffix is empty if the K-th block reaches the end of the string.

3. Build and print the string in this order: the original prefix, the K-th block, the intervening zeros, and the original suffix. The same boundaries work when K is 2, when either block has length one, and when the suffix is empty.

> Only three boundaries are needed to assemble the answer, and the four pieces of the result have a combined length of N.

4. The scan takes O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Constructing the pieces and joining them takes O(N) time and O(N) space for the temporary substrings and result, so the overall time and space are both O(N).

generation.note: Harness wall time includes Codex startup; not API latency.

usage.note: Codex token counts include its harness context; not comparable to API usage.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
